title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Broncos D/ST dismal in loss Monday
items.desc: The Broncos' D/ST logged two sacks and one interception while allowing 31 points in Monday night's blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Denver's defense is supposed to be among the best in the entire NFL, but they didn't look the part on Monday night. They allowed Patrick Mahomes II to lead Kansas City to 31 points on the night, despite the fact that this was his first game back from a major injury and was missing one of his starting tackles. This unit should return to elite form at some point this season, but they have a rocky schedule coming up for the next 4-6 weeks and should not be considered an elite fantasy option at the position for that stretch of games.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Wil Lutz scores four points in loss Monday
items.desc: Wil Lutz made his lone field-goal attempt and his lone extra-point attempt in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Lutz did all that he could on Monday night, making both of his kicks in what turned out to be a blowout loss for the Broncos. He should return to being a decent fantasy option in games where the Broncos are able to move the ball more effectively moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Marvin Mims Jr. entirely uninvolved in loss Monday
items.desc: Marvin Mims Jr. did not see a single offensive opportunity in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: There was a time where it looked like Mims had the potential to be a relevant fantasy option, but that ship has long sailed, which was confirmed by the zero opportunities he saw on Monday night. He didn't see even a single snap on offense, meaning that he should be considered entirely irrelevant for fantasy moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Franklin doesn't contribute in loss Monday
items.desc: Troy Franklin failed to catch his lone target and had one rush for five yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: It was no surprise that Franklin was uninvolved for the Broncos on Monday night, as their offense struggled heavily to get even their best players the ball against the Chiefs. He seems to be squarely behind at least three other wideouts on the depth chart at this point, however, which makes him irrelevant from a fantasy perspective until further notice.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Evan Engram hauls in touchdown Monday
items.desc: Evan Engram caught 4-f-5 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Engram was one of Denver's lone bright spots on offense on Monday night. He caught all but one of his targets against the Chiefs, including one that accounted for the Broncos' lone touchdown in this matchup. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant moving forward, however, and should remain on the waiver wire in most leagues.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Pat Bryant leads team in receiving Monday
items.desc: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-6 targets for 42 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Bryant was one of the few Broncos who had a respectable showing on Monday night. He looked great at the start of the game but tapered off as it went on and as Denver continued to fall further and further behind on the scoreboard. He was the best out of Denver's receivers in this bad matchup, however, so the breakout potential seems to be there for the second-year wideout this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jonah Coleman without attempt in NFL debut Monday
items.desc: Jonah Coleman did not see a single opportunity in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: There has been a lot of hype about the potential of the rookie over the course of the offseason, but he didn't see even a single opportunity in the three snaps he played in his NFL debut on Monday night. He will likely see involvement in more favorable matchups moving forward, but this start is very discouraging and indicates that he is squarely behind both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in the pecking order at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: RJ Harvey totals 41 yards in loss Monday
items.desc: RJ Harvey rushed the ball three times for 18 yards and caught four passes for 23 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The young running back was one of Denver's more effective offensive players on Monday night, which isn't saying much considering he finished with just 41 scoreless yards in the team's loss to the Chiefs. It looks like J.K. Dobbins will be the team's top rushing option this season, but it's encouraging to see Harvey's involvement in the passing game in Week 1, which is his path to relevance over the course of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Courtland Sutton uninvolved in loss Monday
items.desc: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for just 11 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily on Monday night, and Sutton was no exception to that. He caught just two of his five targets over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into a measly 11 yards. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: J.K. Dobbins underwhelming in loss Monday
items.desc: J.K. Dobbins rushed the ball eight times for 36 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Dobbins wasn't able to get much going on Monday night, being left with just 36 scoreless yards in a loss to the Chiefs. The game script was entirely unfavorable to his role, however, with Denver quickly abandoning the run after falling behind early in the game. He should be more involved than this in most games moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaylen Waddle disappoints in Broncos debut Monday
items.desc: Jaylen Waddle caught 1-of-3 targets for just two yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: There has been a lot of hype for the veteran wideout after the Broncos traded for him this offseason, but he got off to a poor start with his new team on Monday night. He caught one pass for just two yards over the course of the game, which burned any fantasy manager who risked starting him in this matchup. Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily against Kansas City's defense, however, so there's a good chance that he and the rest of the offense bounce back and return to solid fantasy production in easier matchups moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Bo Nix struggles in loss Monday
items.desc: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passing attempts for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Nix had a poor performance on Monday night. He was held to just 131 passing yards on the night and wasn't able to get Denver's offense going, leading them to score just ten points en route to a blowout loss at the hands of their divisional rivals. He should improve and play better in more favorable matchups moving forward, but they will continue to have a tough schedule for the foreseeable future, so fantasy managers might be better off looking for another option for the time being.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chiefs D/ST stellar in win Monday
items.desc: The Chiefs' D/ST logged four sacks and one interception while allowing just ten points in Monday night's win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Kansas City was able to pick up a great win over their divisional rivals on Monday night. The performance of their defense had a lot to do with that, as they held Bo Nix and Co. to just ten points on the night and made numerous big plays to help out their offense. This is one of the league's best units at this point, and they will enjoy one of the league's easiest schedules over the next three weeks. They should be a waiver target in any league they are not currently rostered in.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Harrison Butker perfect in win Monday
items.desc: Harrison Butker went 4-for-4 on his extra-point attempts and made his lone field-goal attempt in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Butker did his job on Monday night, hitting all five of his kicks in the team's big win over the Broncos. He didn't end up with a good total from a fantasy perspective, but he should still be considered one of the better fantasy options at his position moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cyrus Allen held catchless in win Monday
items.desc: Cyrus Allen did not haul in his lone target in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: The rookie was silent in his NFL debut on Monday, being held without a catch in the team's big win over the Broncos. They didn't need to pass much in this matchup, so it's possible that he will improve and play better in closer games moving forward. Still, this was a discouraging debut from a utilization standpoint, and fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyquan Thornton silent in win Monday
items.desc: Tyquan Thornton failed to catch his single target in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Thornton showed a lot of promise in Kansas City's offense last year, but he is off to a rough start in 2026, being held without a catch in the team's first game of the season. He may get more involved as QB Patrick Mahomes II continues to knock the rust off after missing significant time with a knee injury, but fantasy managers shouldn't count on him being a consistent contributor at any point this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Emmett Johnson totals 68 yards in NFL debut Monday
items.desc: Emmett Johnson rushed the ball eight times for 24 yards and caught two passes for 44 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: The rookie looked good in his NFL debut on Monday night, totaling 68 yards on ten opportunities against one of the NFL's best defensive fronts. Kenneth Walker III is clearly the bellcow running back on this offense, but it looks like Johnson has solidified himself as the RB2 and will continue to play an important depth role for the Chiefs over the course of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Xavier Worthy quiet in win Monday
items.desc: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Worthy was Kansas City's most targeted player on Monday night, but he wasn't able to do much with his opportunities, finishing with just three catches for 18 yards against the Broncos. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Travis Kelce solid in win Monday
items.desc: Travis Kelce caught 3-of-5 targets for 71 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Kelce wasn't very involved for much of Monday night's game, but he was able to haul in a big catch at one point that helped to leave him with a solid 71 yards on the night. Fantasy managers should be pleased with his performance in this matchup but should not expect him to be a TE1 on a week-to-week basis for the foreseeable future, especially with Kansas City seemingly wanting to operate as a run-heavy team this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rashee Rice finds end zone in win Monday
items.desc: Rashee Rice caught two passes for 19 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Rice had an underwhelming game on Monday night. He was held to just two catches for 19 yards against the Broncos, but he was able to get into the end zone on one of those receptions, which helped to salvage his fantasy total. QB Patrick Mahomes II didn't look his way very much in this game, but it seems like the team wanted Mahomes to drop back as little as possible given that it was his first game back from a major knee injury. Rice will likely improve going forward, but fantasy managers should keep a close eye on his production over the next few weeks to gauge whether this poor showing was a fluke or a sign of the things to come for the veteran wideout this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kenneth Walker III dominant in win Monday
items.desc: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown while catching 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards and an additional touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Walker was absolutely dominant in his debut with the Chiefs on Monday night. He totaled 191 yards and two touchdowns over the course of the game, which was especially impressive considering that he did it against one of the best defenses in the NFL in the Broncos. He looks great on his new offense and should be in line for a huge season if he can stay healthy with this increased workload.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Patrick Mahomes II scores three touchdowns in return game Monday
items.desc: Patrick Mahomes II completed 15-of-27 passing attempts for 184 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception while adding 23 yards and a touchdown on the ground in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Monday night marked Mahomes' first game back after suffering a serious knee injury that ended his 2025 season prematurely. He looked good in his first game back, totaling over 200 yards and scoring three touchdowns on the night, including one impressive rushing touchdown from over ten yards out. He and Kansas City's offense as a whole are looking promising right now and may be primed for a big season if they can stay healthy this year.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) out for remainder of Monday night
items.desc: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) has been ruled out for the rest of the Chiefs game against Denver on Monday night.
items.impact: Delane had a pick against Bo Nix early, but got knocked out of the game shortly after. He will now focus on trying to get back onto the field for the Chiefs Week 2 contest.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Sam Darnold dealing with 'unique' soft-tissue injury
items.desc: The Seahawks say Sam Darnold has a "very unique" soft-tissue injury.
items.impact: Darnold's hip joint is unaffected. It is considered a short-term injury, meaning likely less than four weeks with him avoiding injured reserve.

items.impact: It is a short week for Buffalo playing on Thursday. Sanders will have to be monitored in practice the next couple of days.

items.desc: Ty Johnson was a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
items.impact: It is a short week for Buffalo playing on Thursday. Johnson will have to be monitored in practice the next couple of days.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jordan Hancock (quad) logs full practice Monday
items.desc: Jordan Hancock was a full participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
items.impact: Hancock should be good to go despite it being a short week for Buffalo.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Bradley Chubb (thumb) logs full practice Monday
items.desc: Bradley Chubb was a full participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
items.impact: Chubb should be good to go despite it being a short week for Buffalo.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Cole Bishop (knee/groin) logs full practice Monday
items.desc: Cole Bishop was a full participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
items.impact: Bishop should be good to go on a short week despite dealing with multiple injuries.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Terrel Bernard (calf) estimated as limited practice Monday
items.desc: Terrel Bernard was estimated as a limited participant in practice on Monday.
items.impact: Bernard is on the injury report with a calf issue. He is likely to play on Thursday against the Lions.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Christian Izien (groin) logs full practice Monday
items.desc: Christian Izien was a full participant in Monday's estimated practice.
items.impact: Izien did not play in Week 1. He will have a chance to play on Thursday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Juice Scruggs (knee) limited in practice Monday
items.desc: Juice Scruggs was estimated as a limited participant in practice on Monday.
items.impact: It is an estimated injury report. Detroit has a short week playing on Thursday against the Bills.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Blake Miller (knee) estimated as missing practice Monday
items.desc: Blake Miller was estimated as a non-participant in practice on Monday.
items.impact: Miller is on the injury report with a knee issue. It is a short week for Detroit.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Christian Mahogany (hip) estimated as missing practice Monday
items.desc: Christian Mahogany was estimated as a non-participant in practice on Monday.
items.impact: Mahogany left Sunday's game early with a knee injury. His status is uncertain on a short week.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Trey Smith (hip) active for Week 1
items.desc: Trey Smith (hip) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Smith will suit up after increasing practice activity throughout the week, providing a boost to a Kansas City offensive line without tackle Josh Simmons (back) against a disruptive Denver defensive front Monday night.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Josh Simmons (back) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Josh Simmons (back) is inactive for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Simmons will not suit up for the Monday night divisional matchup after struggling to practice throughout the week, with rookie Kahlil Benson set to protect quarterback Patrick Mahomes against an aggressive Denver defensive front Monday night.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Landon Dickerson placed on IR
items.desc: The Eagles placed OL Landon Dickerson on injured reserve.
items.impact: McLane notes that Dickerson had been playing with various ailments. He will miss at least the next four games.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Isiah Pacheco (back/knee) out for 12 weeks after undergoing back surgery
items.desc: Isiah Pacheco (back/knee) is out for at least the next 12 weeks after undergoing surgery to remove a body that was pressing a nerve on his neck. The plan is to have him back in early December.
items.impact: It's a tough blow to Pacheco, who was already struggling with a knee injury. He's droppable in all formats, as his handcuff status for 2026 is pretty much out the window.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Ladd McConkey (rib) to be monitored this week
items.desc: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey is dealing a rib injury and he'll be monitored throughout the week.
items.impact: McConkey was further evaluated on Monday for his injury. His status is uncertain heading into Week 2 against the Raiders.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Brock Bowers (knee) considered day-to-day
items.desc: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers is day-to-day.
items.impact: Bowers did not play in Sunday's season opener after undergoing a meniscus trim. His status remains uncertain for Week 2.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) considered day-to-day
items.desc: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said WR Zay Flowers is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury.
items.impact: It is a good sign after Flowers left Sunday's game early after a very strong first half. His status for Week 2 still remains uncertain.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Frankie Luvu suffers groin injury
items.desc: Frankie Luvu suffered a groin injury in Sunday's loss against the Eagles.
items.impact: The status of Luvu will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jordan Magee suffers hamstring injury
items.desc: Jordan Magee is dealing with a hamstring injury from Sunday's loss against the Eagles.
items.impact: Magee pulled his hamstring trying to chase down Jalen Hurts on his long scramble in the fourth quarter. His status will need to be monitored in practice.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Chris Lindstrom placed in concussion protocol
items.desc: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said RG Chris Lindstrom is in concussion protocol.
items.impact: Lindstrom will have to clear all protocols later in the week to be available for Week 2.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) without update on status
items.desc: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski did not have any updates on Monday regarding the team's quarterback situation.
items.impact: Tagovailoa was not available in Sunday's loss against the Steelers. The status of both him and Michael Penix Jr. will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) without update on status
items.desc: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski did not have any updates on Monday regarding the team's quarterback situation.
items.impact: Penix was not available in Sunday's loss against the Steelers. The status of both him and Tua Tagovailoa will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Alec Pierce suffers hand/wrist bruise, expected to be fine
items.desc: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce's left hand/wrist is fine.
items.impact: Pierce said he is dealing with a bruise. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.
